summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted with hematochezia and chest pain. He reported three days of maroon stools and acute-onset epigastric and chest pain similar to a prior admission. He remained hemodynamically stable but required three transfusions for acute on chronic blood loss anemia. Upper endoscopy revealed non-bleeding pyloric ulcers, and colonoscopy identified a benign-appearing transverse colon polyp and hemorrhoids, with incomplete visualization due to residual stool. Capsule endoscopy was attempted but failed as the capsule initially remained in the stomach, though it later passed into the colon. His chest pain resolved and was attributed to demand ischemia from anemia rather than acute coronary syndrome. He was discharged home with stable vital signs, new prescriptions including isosorbide mononitrate, and plans for outpatient GI and cardiology follow-up for polyp removal, repeat capsule endoscopy, and evaluation for beta blockade.
problems: Gastric ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
